questions.question_text: A caterer got a contract to cook food for a one-day event. To make his signature dish, a caterer takes quantities of rice A, rice B and rice C in the ratio 2:2:1 respectively. The cost are ₹40/kg, ₹50/kg and ₹30/kg of rice A, rice B and rice C respectively. The rest of the ensemble in a plate costs the caterer ₹350/plate. The caterer has taken the utensils to prepare the food on rent at ₹5000/day and the wait staff costs him ₹20000/day. The event is for 250 people and the caterer wants to make a profit of 50% from the event. How much should he charge per plate to get his desired profit ? Assume that the total consumption of rice in the event will be 250 kgs.
questions.solution_text:
For this scenario, we need to find the total cost of the food borne by the caterer and divide it by the number of plates to arrive at the cost per plate. Here, we also need to add the cost of the utensils on rent as well as the cost of the wait staff involved.  
So, cost of 5 kgs of signature dish = (2 x 40)+(2 x 50)+(1 x 30) = ₹210 
Thus, cost of preparing 1 kg of the signature dish = $\dfrac{210}{5} = ₹42$/kg 
Total cost of the signature dish = 42 x 250 = ₹10500
Total cost of ensemble in the plate = 350 x 250 = ₹87500
Overall cost of the event for the caterer = 10500+87500+5000+20000 = ₹123000
Thus, cost per plate to the caterer = $\dfrac{123000}{250} = ₹492$/plate
If the caterer wants a profit of 50%, then the selling price of the plate = $(1 + \frac{50}{100}) \times 492$
$ \Rightarrow \frac{3}{2} \times 492 = ₹738$
Thus the caterer should price the food at ₹738/plate.

questions.question_text: Train A starts from P towards Q and train B starts from Q towards P on two parallel rail tracks. Irrespective of the time at which train A starts it reaches Q at 7:00 PM. Similarly, B follows a strict schedule of reaching P at 5:00 PM. When A started at 1:00 PM and B started at 2:00 PM, both the trains met at R. After this meeting, train A took t minutes to reach Q. Find the value of t.
questions.solution_text:
Since train A travels the distance between P and Q in 6 hours and train B travels this distance in 3 hours. The ratio of their speed will be 
$\frac{d\times\ 3}{6\times\ d}$ = 1:2 (d is the distance between P and Q)
Assume the speed of A is v km/hr and the speed of B =  2v km/hr
Then from 1 PM to 2 PM, A will travel v*1 = v km
Assume train A is at point M, when it is 2:00 PM.
At this time train B starts.
So time taken to cover MR by A will be the time taken to cover QR by B. Assume this time is m hours.
=> B covers RP in 3-m hours. (Total time taken to cover PQ = 3 hours)
=> RP = 2v(3-m)  ....(1)
Now, time taken by A to cover RP = time taken to cover PM + time taken to cover MR = 1 PM to 2 PM + m = 1+m
Hence, RP = v(1+m) .....(2)
Equating 1 and 2, we get
2v(3-m)=v(1+m)    => 6-2m=1+m   =>m=$\frac{5}{3}$ hours
Time taken by A to cover RQ = Total time - time taken to cover PM - Time taken to cover MR = 6-1-$\frac{5}{3}$ = $\frac{10}{3}$
Hence, t  = $\frac{10}{3}\times\ 60\ =\ 200$ minutes

questions.question_text: Raman has to distribute 18 identical pens among 4 of students Kiran, Kartik, Kamal and Kishor. He has to make sure that Kartik gets at least 3 and at most 8 pens. In how many ways this can be done?
questions.solution_text:
Let 'a', 'b', 'c' and 'd' be the number of pens received by Kiran, Kartik, Kamal and Kishor respectively. 
$\therefore$ a + b + c + d = 18.
Case 1: When Kartik gets at least 3 pens. 
To find out the number of ways when Kartik gets at least 9 pens we will have to replace c by c'+3. 
$\therefore$ a + b + c' + 3 + d = 18
$\Rightarrow$ a + b + c' + d = 15
Hence, total number of ways so that Kartik gets at least 3 pens = (15+4-1)C(4-1) = 18C3.
Case 2: When Kartik get at least 9 pens. 
To find out the number of ways when Kartik gets at least 9 pens we will have to replace c by c'+9. 
$\therefore$ a + b + c' + 9 + d = 18
$\Rightarrow$ a + b + c' + d = 9
Hence, total number of ways so that Kartik gets at least 9 pens = (9+4-1)C(4-1) = 12C3.
Therefore, the total number of ways Kartik gets at least 3 and at most 8 pens = 18C3 - 12C3 = 816 - 220 = 596.

questions.question_text: A sells an object to B at a profit of 20% who sells it to C at a profit of 20%. C sells it to D at a loss of 10% who sells it to E at a loss of 12.5%. E sells the object back to A at no profit or loss. A sells it back to F at the same cost he bought it for in the first instance. If A makes a profit of Rs.33 in the process, find the initial cost price of the object.
questions.solution_text:
Let the cost of the object for A be $x$
Selling price of the object for A = Cost price of the object for B = $\dfrac{6}{5} \times x = \dfrac{6x}{5}$ 
Selling price of the object for B = Cost price of the object for C = $\dfrac{6x}{5} \times \dfrac{6}{5} = \dfrac{36x}{25} $ 
Selling price of the object for C = Cost price of the object for D = $\dfrac{36x}{25} \times \dfrac{9}{10} = \dfrac{162x}{125} $ 
Selling price of the object for D = Cost price of the object for E = $\dfrac{162x}{125} \times \dfrac{7}{8} = \dfrac{567x}{500} $ 
Selling price of the object for E = Cost price of the object for A = $\dfrac{567x}{500} $ 
Selling price of the object for A = Cost price of the object for F = $x$ 
Total Profit made by A = Total amount of money earned - Total amount of money paid 
$ \Rightarrow 33 = (\dfrac{6x}{5}+x) - (\dfrac{567x}{500} + x) $ 
$ \Rightarrow 33 = \dfrac{33x}{500} $ 
$ \Rightarrow x = 33 \times \dfrac{500}{33} $ 
$ \Rightarrow x = 500 $

Grandson's age= x
Manoj's age =15x
Son's age =5x
Manoj's father's age =15x+20
The mean age of all the four family members = 50. 
x + 15x+5x+15x+20= 50*4
36x=180
x=5
Grandson's age= 5
Manoj's age =75

questions.question_text: Two friends P and Q have a certain amount of money with them in denominations of Rs 2 and Rs 5. The total number of coins with P and Q are 21 and 22 respectively. The amount of money with P is Rs 20 less than that with Q. The total value of money in the denomination of Rs 5 is 90. Find the ratio of the number of Rs 2 coins with P to that of Rs 5 coins with Q.
questions.solution_text:
Assuming the number of Rs 2 coins with P = p, then the number of Rs 5 coins = 21-p
Amount of money with P = 2p+5(21-p) = 105-3p
Assuming the number of Rs 2 coins with Q = q, then the number of Rs 5 coins = 22-q
Amount of money with Q = 2q+5(22-q) = 110-3q
The amount of money with P is Rs 20 less than that with Q.
=> 110-3q-(105-3p) = 5-3q+3p =20
=> 3p-3q = 15
=> p-q = 5......(1)
Total value of money in denomination of Rs 5 = 90
Hence the total number of Rs 5 coins = 90/5 = 18 which is also equal to 21-p+22-q
=> 43-p-q=18  =>p+q = 25 ....(2)
From 1 and 2, p =15, q = 10
Required ratio = $\frac{p}{22-q}=\frac{15}{22-10}=\frac{5}{4}$

questions.question_text: Ram and Shyam started running to and fro on a straight track AB from point A at the same time, each of them running with a constant speed throughout.Their first meet took place at a point P located at 960m from A and their second meet took place at a point Q located at 720m from B. They were going in opposite directions when they met for the second time. Find the distance of the point from B where they meet for the sixth time.
questions.solution_text:
Let their speeds be V1 &V2 and AB be S metres
Now when they meet for the first time, the distances covered by them would be 960 metres and 2S-960 metres 
Now we know that ratio of speeds = ratio of distances (as time is constant)
Therefore $\frac{V1}{V2}=\frac{960}{2S-960}$ (1)
Now, similarly when they meet for the 2nd time, the distances covered by them would be S+720metres and 3S-720metres
now their speed ratio would be :$\frac{V1}{V2}=\frac{S+720}{3S-720}$ (2)
Now we can equate both equations 1 & 2 as speed ratio will be same 
Therefore we get $\frac{960}{2s-960}=\frac{S+720}{3S-720}$
solving we get S =1200 
Therefore $\frac{V1}{V2}=\frac{960}{1440}$=$\frac{2}{3}$
Now when they meet for the 6th time total distance covered by them would be $\left(12\times\ 1200\right)$
(as for every 1 meet they cover 2S=2*1200 metres together)
Therefore Distance covered by one which is slower =$\frac{2}{5}\times\ 1200\times\ 12$=5760metres
Now 5760=4800+960
Therefore meet will take place at 960metres from A or 1200-960=240metres from B 
Hence answer is 240metres from B

If $\frac{1}{p+r}+\frac{1}{q+r}=\frac{3}{p+q+r}$, then tan(R) equals
questions.solution_text:
Given equation is $\frac{1}{p+r}+\frac{1}{q+r}=\frac{3}{p+q+r}$
=> $\frac{\left(p+q+2r\right)}{\left(p+r\right)\left(q+r\right)}=\frac{3}{p+q+r}$

=> $p^2+q^2-r^2=pq$
=> $\frac{\left(p^2+q^2-r^2\right)}{2pq}=\frac{1}{2}=\cos\left(R\right)$
=> $R=60^{\circ\ }$
=> $\tan\left(R\right)=\sqrt{\ 3}$

questions.question_text: The ratio of the total surface area to the lateral surface area of an equilateral triangular prism is 3:1. What is the ratio of the height of the prism to the side of its base?
questions.solution_text:
Let the side of the base be a units and height of the prism be h units
TSA = perimeter of the base * height + 2*area of the base = 3ah + $\frac{\sqrt{\ 3}}{2}a^2$
LSA = perimeter of the base * height = 3ah
$\frac{TSA}{LSA}=\frac{\left(3ah+\frac{\sqrt{\ 3}}{2}a^2\right)}{3ah}$ = 3
=> $1+\frac{a}{2\sqrt{\ 3}h}=3$
=>$\frac{a}{h}=4\sqrt{\ 3}$
Hence$\frac{h}{a}=1:4\sqrt{\ 3}$

questions.solution_text:
Let the amount be P.

CI = P(1.1)(1.2)(1.1)(1.2) - P = 0.7424P

questions.question_text: A starts running from a point X in a straight line at a speed of 21.6 km/hr. After 30 seconds, B starts running from X in the same direction as A. Speed of A is 20% more than the speed of B. 90 seconds after B started running from X, C starts from X with a speed 40% more than that of B. What is the difference between the time when C overtakes B and when C overtakes A ?
questions.solution_text:
Let the speeds of A,B,C be $a$,$b$,$c$ respectively. 
Here, $a = 21.6 = \dfrac{108}{5} \times \dfrac{5}{18} = 6$ m/s 
We know that, $b + \dfrac{b}{5} = a \Rightarrow b = a \times \dfrac{5}{6} $ 
$ \Rightarrow b = 6 \times \dfrac{5}{6} = 5$m/s
Now, $c = \dfrac{7}{5} \times b = 7$m/s 
C starts 90 seconds after B which is 30+90 = 120 seconds after A. 
When C starts, distance covered by A = 120 x 6 = 720 m 
When C starts, distance covered by B = 90 x 5 = 450 m 
Relative speed of C and B = 7-5 = 2 m/s 
Time taken by C to overtake B = $\dfrac{450}{2} $ = 225 seconds 
Relative speed of C and A = 7-6 = 1 m/s 
Time taken by C to overtake A = $\dfrac{720}{1} $ = 720 seconds 
Difference between the two times = 720 - 225 = 495 seconds = 8 mins 15 secs

questions.question_text: The sum of an infinite geometric progression is 5. If all the terms are of the GP are raised to the power 3, the sum of resulting series is 375. Then the common ratio of the GP is
questions.solution_text:
Assuming the first term = a and the common ratio = r.
The sum = a/(1-r) = 5 ....(1)
Now after raising to the power 3, sum = a$^{3}$/(1-r$^{3}$) = 375 ....(2)
After raising both sides of (1) to the power 3 and dividing by (2), we get
(1+r+r$^{2}$)/(1-2r+r$^{2}$) = 1/3
=> 3+3r+3r$^{2}$ = 1-2r+r$^{2}$
=> 2r$^{2}$+5r+2=0
=> r=-1/2  or r=-2, 
Since GP is infinite, hence r=-2 will be rejected.

Another circle C2 is drawn such that it touches the lines MO, LO and the circle C1. What is the ratio of the area of C2 to the area of the square ABCD?
questions.solution_text:
Let the sides of the square be 2a, and the radius of the circle C2= r.

Radius of the circle C1=a
PO= LO= a
PO = r + r$\sqrt{\ 2}$
a= $r\left(1+\sqrt{\ 2}\right)$
The ratio of the area of C2 to the area of the square ABCD= $\frac{\pi\ r^2}{\left(2a\right)^2}$
=$\frac{\pi\ r^2}{4\left(r\left(\sqrt{\ 2}+1\right)\right)^2}$
=$\frac{\pi\ }{4\left(3+2\sqrt{\ 2}\right)}$
Option A

$\frac{1}{2}$*10$\sqrt{2}$*AB$\sin45^0$ = 200
AB=40 units
Now let us draw a perpendicular from vertices C and D to AB,
The lengths of AP and PD should be equal, (A =$45^0$)
$AP^2 + PD^2$ = 200

questions.question_text: A tank has 8 filling pipes and 8 draining pipes. All the filling pipes fill at the same rate, while all the draining pipes drain at the same rate. If all 16 pipes are on, the tank will get filled in 30 hours. If 5 pipes of one type are on and 3 pipes of another are on it will take 10 hours. What is the approximate time it will take to fill the tank if 4 draining pipes are on and 5 filling pipes are on?
questions.solution_text:
Let the efficiency of filling pipes be 'x' and the efficiency of draining pipes be '-y'.
In the first case, 
Capacity of tank = (8x - 8y) * 30..........(i)
In the second case,
Capacity of tank = (5x - 3y) * 10.....(ii)
Or Capacity of tank = (3x - 5y) * 10.....(iii)
Case 1: On equating (i) and (ii), we get
(8x - 8y) * 30 = (5x - 3y) * 10
or, 24x - 24y = 5x - 3y
or, 19x = 21y
Case 2: On equating (i) and (iii), we get
(8x - 8y) * 30 = (3x - 5y) * 10
or, 24x - 24y = 3x - 5y
or, 21x = 19y
This case is not possible since draining pipes drain faster than filling pipes. In this case, if an equal number of draining and filling pipes were on the tank would never be filled. However, it is given in the question that when 8 draining pipes and 8 filling pipes are on the tank fills in 30 hours. 
So, consider only the first case.
Capacity of the tank = (8x - 8y) * 30 = ($\frac{21}{19}$y - y) * 240 = $\frac{480}{19}$y
Net efficiency of 5 filling and 4 draining pipes = (5x - 4y) = (5$\frac{21}{19}$y - 4y) = $\frac{29}{19}y$
Time required = $\dfrac{\text{480y}}{\text{29y}}$ hours
= 16 hours and 33 minutes.
Hence, Option C is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: The densities of three elements A, B, C are 5, 10 and 15 gm/ml respectively. A and B are mixed in equal ratio by volume to form a compound D. C and D are mixed in some weight ratio to form a compound E. If the density of E is 10 gm/ml, calculate the weight ratio in which C and D are mixed.
questions.solution_text:
A and B are mixed in equal volumes, that is, in a 1:1 ratio.$\frac{\left(5+10\right)}{2}=7.5$
So the density of D is 7.5 gm/ml. Let the ratio of C and D by volume be x:1 =>$\frac{\left(15x+7.5\right)}{(x+1)}=10$ => x = 1/2. Therefore, the weight ratio is $\frac{1}{2}\cdot15:1\cdot7.5$ = 1:1.

questions.question_text: What is the remainder when 123123123123....(298 digits) is divided by 9?
questions.solution_text:
To find the remainder when a number N is divided by 9, we have to find the digital sum of N first.
Digital Sum = 1+2+3+....+1+2+3+1 = 99(1+2+3)+1 = 595
595 mod 9 = 1   <----remainder

questions.question_text: In a leap year, what is the probability that a day that starts with 'T' comes 53 times?
questions.solution_text:
A leap year has only 2 days that appear more than 52 times. 
There are a total of seven cases.
The year starts on Monday. The additional days are M and T.
The year starts on Tuesday. The additional days are T and W.
The year starts on Wednesday. The additional days are W and T.
The year starts on Thursday. The additional days are T and F.
The year starts on Friday. The additional days are F and S.
The year starts on Saturday. The additional days are S and S.
The year starts on Sunday. The additional days are S and M.
P = 4/7.
